result.topic_en: Gauss states a general theorem to be proved about the auxiliary equation of degree e whose roots are the periods (sums of p-th roots of unity) of f terms modulo a prime p, using p=43, 42=3·14 as example, claiming its roots are real residues modulo m when m^e ≡ 1 mod p; below is a German note solving a linear Diophantine equation.
result.transcription:
Theorema generale demonstrandum.

1. Sit $p$ primus et si fieri potest discerpatur
$p-1$ in factores $e, f$ E. gr. $43 = p$; $42 = 3 \cdot 14$.

2. His positis semper datur aequatio gradus $\underline{e}$, cuius
radices sunt $\Sigma (\sqrt[p]{1})^{\varrho^{k}}$ term. $\underline{f}$ mod. $\underline{p}$. nostro casu
datur aequatio $x^3 + Axx + Bx + C = 0$ cuius radices
sunt [-$1/ \; 1 + \varrho^3 + \varrho^6 \ldots + \varrho^{39}$
$2/ \; \varrho + \varrho^4 + \varrho^7 \ldots + \varrho^{40}$
$3/ \; \varrho\varrho + \varrho^5 + \varrho^8 \ldots + \varrho^{41}$-]

$1)$ $\varepsilon + \varepsilon^{(\varrho^3)} + \varepsilon^{(\varrho^6)} + \varepsilon^{(\varrho^9)} + \ldots \varepsilon^{(\varrho^{39})}$ ubi $\varepsilon = \sqrt[p]{1}$
$2)$ $\varepsilon^{\varrho} + \varepsilon^{\varrho^4} + \varepsilon^{\varrho^7} + \ldots$ $\varrho$ radix elem.
$3)$ $\varepsilon^{\varrho\varrho} + \varepsilon^{\varrho^5} + +$ modulo existente $p$

Dico hanc aequationem habere omnes radices (resid: f.)
reales posito modulo quocunque $\underline{m}$ quando $m^e \equiv 1$ modulo
$p$.

Oder $y = \frac{25-2x}{3}$ Also darf $x$ nicht über 12 seyn. Man dividire wirklich:
so erhält man $y = 8 - \frac{2x-1}{3}$ Also $2x-1$ durch 3 theilbar. Man setze
$2x-1 = 3z$ oder $x = (z+1):2$. $z$ muss also ungerade, u. da $x$ nicht über 12
seyn darf, nicht über 23 u. in 3 theilbar seyn. Also

$z = 3$ | $z = 9$ | $z = 15$ | $z = 21$
$x = 2$ | $x = 5$ | $x = 8$ | $x = 11$
$y = 7$ | $y = 5$ | $y = 3$ | $y = 1$ Welches der andern Art völlig entspricht.

[Bemerkung zum Tgb.[?]; vgl. [?] S. 9. 5.11[?]]

methods.what: Gaussian periods: roots of the degree-e auxiliary equation are sums of f p-th roots of unity with exponents running over powers of a primitive root
Factorization p-1 = e·f to define periods (example p=43, 42=3·14), giving a cubic
Solving linear Diophantine equation 2x+3y=25 in positive integers by division and substitution
